title: 60-240 Hz is the accepted measured timestep envelope for the calibrated contact fixture and 30 Hz is causally rejected
claim: For the exact L1.5 physical-time-preserving dynamic drop plus static eccentric pad fixture, physics rates 60, 120, and 240 Hz form the contiguous accepted measured interval while 30 Hz is rejected with causal evidence: touch/load timing of 0.6667 s against an analytic expectation of approximately 0.4949 s, maximum penetration of approximately 95.78 mm, and a settled height approximately 20 mm too low. Unmeasured rates cannot be interpolated and no universal minimum physics rate is claimed.
scope: The preregistered L1.5 drop-and-settle contact fixture at exactly 30, 60, 120, and 240 Hz with physical time preserved across rates, first-principles timing, speed, and impulse gates, TOUCH/LOAD phase separation, fresh evidence per rate, Godot 4.7 Jolt backend.
mechanism: Contact resolution quality depends on how far a body can travel and penetrate within one step. At 30 Hz the fixture's contact events land a full measured interval late relative to the analytic free-fall time, penetration grows to tens of millimeters, and the settled pose is biased low, so the 30 Hz cell fails the preregistered physical gates while 60-240 Hz pass them.
applicability: Choosing a physics tick rate for later lab fixtures of this contact class
Rejecting low-rate configurations before they contaminate contact evidence
failure_boundaries: Does not establish a universal minimum physics rate for every creature or mechanism
Does not cover unmeasured rates between or beyond the grid; interpolation is forbidden
Does not cover articulated chains, joints, or high-speed impacts beyond the fixture
Does not establish standing, bracing, fall arrest, getting up, or walking

parameter_effects.change: decrease from the accepted 60-240 Hz interval to the measured 30 Hz cell
parameter_effects.affects: contact timing, penetration depth, and settled height
parameter_effects.mechanism: Longer steps let the falling body traverse and penetrate farther before the solver responds, delaying touch/load events and biasing the settled pose
hinges_on: Physical time being preserved across rate cells
The fixture's mass, drop height, and geometry staying pinned

minimal_repair_rules.symptom: Contact events land late and penetration is tens of millimeters deep in a lab fixture of this class
minimal_repair_rules.diagnosis: The physics tick rate sits outside the measured accepted envelope for this fixture class
minimal_repair_rules.smallest_change: Raise physics_ticks_per_second into the measured 60-240 Hz interval
minimal_repair_rules.expected_effect: Touch/load timing and penetration return inside the preregistered gates
do_not_apply_when: The fixture class, speeds, or masses differ enough that the envelope was never measured for it

unknowns: Whether the envelope holds for articulated chains and fast swing-phase contacts
Where the true failure boundary sits between 30 and 60 Hz
Whether rates above 240 Hz change solved outcomes for this fixture
